hook: The emperor who built Hagia Sophia and wrote down Roman law.

pages.x: Justinian was born around 482 to a peasant family in the Balkans. His uncle Justin, a farm boy who rose to command the palace guard, became emperor in 518 and brought him to Constantinople to be educated. Justinian took the throne in 527.

He married Theodora, a former actress, a scandalous job at the time; a law had to be changed to allow it. She became his closest adviser. In the Nika riots of 532, when he was ready to flee the city, she said: "Royalty is a fine burial shroud." He stayed, and the riot was crushed.

The rioters had burned the great church of the city. Justinian rebuilt it as Hagia Sophia, "Holy Wisdom", in under six years, with a dome so vast it seemed to hang from heaven. Entering, he is said to have cried: "Solomon, I have outdone you!" For 1,000 years it was the largest church in the world.

He had all of Roman law collected, sorted and simplified into one Body of Civil Law. Rediscovered in Italy around 1070, it became the foundation of law in most of Europe, and in countries from Brazil to Japan.

His general Belisarius took back North Africa from the Vandals, then fought for years to win back Italy from the Goths, and part of Spain was taken too. For a moment the Mediterranean was a Roman lake again.

In 541 the first known outbreak of bubonic plague reached Constantinople and killed perhaps a quarter of its people. Justinian caught it himself, and survived. It came back again and again for two centuries.
Justinian dreamed of rebuilding the Roman Empire. His conquests did not last, but his law code shaped the laws of Europe, and Hagia Sophia still stands in Istanbul.
